title: Database failover and split-brain after a primary dies

hook.shape: A primary database dies overnight and writes stop, framed as a mismatch between a brief glitch and a long outage.

arc: failure hook → failover mechanism → open question → dated incident → split-brain twist → new rule → two-line close

beats.summary: An application writes to a primary database until it dies overnight and the writes stop, framed as a tiny hiccup with a long aftermath.
A follower is handed the leader badge, the other followers re-point to copy from it, and the application's writes re-route to the new primary.
The board dims behind a short question card asking whether the old primary is really gone, and the question is left open.
A sourced, dated case: two regional databases joined through a network hub lose their link, an outage clock runs, and the standby is promoted.
The link returns with both sides holding the leader badge and their own new writes; the divergence is named and the merge turns out to be manual.
A rule label states the new policy the team adopted: no automatic promotion across regions.
A two-line contrast closes the lesson, one line on what is easy and one on what is hard, then a pointer to a longer video appears.

pacing: The failover demo moves fast; the incident and the divergence get the most screen time.
Two still moments: the open question and the closing contrast, both over a dimmed board.
The rule lands straight after the damage is shown, before any summary.
